source_record_claim: Limit behavior of renewal processes (Chinese source wording: 更新过程的极限行为).
statement_ambiguity: The repository record names a theorem and a topic but gives no mathematical formula. It does not select ordinary versus delayed renewal, nonarithmetic versus arithmetic interarrival laws, support on the nonnegative half-line versus a real-valued random walk, the renewal-measure convention, the admissible test-function class, or a zero/infinite-mean boundary. Adopting one standard variant as the root without a pinned source would substitute missing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Unfrozen: a probability law for interarrival times or increments, its renewal measure/function, a real-valued test function, and the time domain must be selected by a source-faithful statement.
conclusion: Unfrozen; the repository description asserts only asymptotic behavior of a renewal process.
candidate_scope_families: Nonarithmetic key renewal theorem on the nonnegative half-line: for a proper interarrival distribution with finite positive mean mu and a directly Riemann integrable test function z, the renewal convolution tends to (1/mu) times the integral of z.
Arithmetic key renewal theorem, whose conclusion is a span-dependent lattice sum rather than the nonarithmetic integral limit.
Random-walk renewal theorem on the real line, with drift and integrability hypotheses that differ from the nonnegative-interarrival formulation.
excluded_scope: No candidate family is adopted as the canonical root at intake.
Blackwell's renewal theorem is the separate manifest target THM-M-1077 and is not substituted for this target.
The elementary renewal theorem or an asymptotic for the renewal counting function alone is not sufficient to discharge the key renewal theorem.
A definition of renewal convolution or an assumption of the desired limit is not proof evidence.
